comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implementation complete (pending Gerrit review). Design decisions of note:

1. Marker ownership: `evidence_sufficient:false` is written ONLY by the framework — the bounded fallback now calls a new `CriterionBank.record_insufficient()` (source="fallback") instead of the model-facing record tool, so the tool stays bool-only and a tool met=false remains a positive refutation. `harvest_structured_into_bank` ignores any model-supplied marker and preserves a prior entry's marker on a markerless met=false overwrite (met=true clears it).

2. Module-size cap: completion_banking.py was at 799/800 LOC, so the verdict-assembly cluster (assemble_deterministic_verdict, merge_finalizer_with_bank, ticket_id_of, _findings_for_unmet) was extracted along its existing call-graph seam into new completion_verdict_assembly.py (258 LOC) with re-exports from completion_banking — no caller changes. banking is now 660 LOC.

3. Authoritative re-stamp: merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps EVERY record from its bank entry via _restamp_marker (stamps a still-unmet echo over a marked entry; strips model-minted markers over bare entries or met=true). Deterministic assembly and both placeholder branches carry the marker; findings say "insufficient evidence", not refutation.

4. reconcile_verdict derives the top-level marker (never trusts model output): set iff FAIL, >=1 unmet record carries the per-criterion marker, and NO unmet record lacks it; such a FAIL carries a new INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_REMEDIATION instead of the generic guidance. PASS pops both. The 2a6f verdict_obtainable fault path is untouched (pinned by test).

5. Sidecar FAIL payload now records `criteria` (previously omitted) plus the top-level marker, mirroring the verdict_obtainable block, so an insufficiency FAIL is diagnosable from the durable record. close_precheck refusal still raises fail-closed but reports "insufficient evidence for N criteria (nothing positively refuted)" when marked. Renderer wording likewise.

6. Complexity ratchet: extracting _verification_fail_message dropped _completion_precheck below the McCabe threshold entirely — the frozen ceiling entry became stale and was removed via the sanctioned shrink-only `--update-stale` path (a decrease, not a bump).

Validation: withheld-oracle TDD — new tests/unit/workflow/test_insufficient_evidence_marker.py (31 tests) written first, 24 failed on unmodified code / 7 regression guards passed; all green after. Manual mutation pass: 24 mutants across every changed function, 24/24 killed. make lint, make typecheck, complexity check (new=0 increased=0 stale=0) all green. Full unit suite: 10368 passed; the only failures are the known environmental git-remote/bare-repo class (fail identically on a clean tree).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Field evidence (validation of this fix's premise): two independent epic closes today hit the exact target failure class. (1) becoming-berserk-grunion close: completion verifier hit step budget (request_limit=24, 95s) and reported 2 ACs unmet that were satisfied on merged main (tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py, e72e comment) — resolved only via [operator-attested] tags + re-verify. (2) The pony-epic session reports the same: budget exhaustion at 32 requests across 15 ACs failed 5 criteria that closed children already satisfy. Both are absence-of-evidence-rendered-as-refutation — precisely what the evidence_sufficient:false marker distinguishes. No design change needed; incidents confirm the bounded-fallback/marker approach.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Design implication (operator-directed): budget exhaustion currently pressures agents into an ANTI-PATTERN — tagging code-verifiable criteria [operator-attested] to bypass the exhausted search (observed in both incidents in the prior comment; both were wrong to tag). This strengthens the case for the evidence_sufficient:false marker: exhaustion must be visibly a verifier-capacity outcome prompting re-verify (or evidence-citation in untagged comments), never a prompt to launder repo-provable criteria into attestations. Remediation text for marker-carrying FAILs should say exactly that: re-verify after making evidence discoverable; do NOT tag code-verifiable criteria as operator-attested.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Verified -1 root cause (change 1788 PS1) + fix (PS2):

Root cause: the audit ticket page (src/rebar/audit/page.py::_completion_section) was a completion-verdict consumer MISSING from the plan's enumerated consumer graph. It discriminated PASS vs FAIL sidecar records by SHAPE — `"criteria" in sidecar` — a proxy that held only because FAIL payloads historically omitted criteria. This change (deliberately, per the certified design) added `criteria[]` to the FAIL sidecar payload so per-criterion evidence_sufficient markers persist; FAIL records then satisfied the shape proxy, took the PASS rendering branch, and the failure findings vanished from the page (tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page_heldout.py::test_completion_fail_renders_failure_findings_fallback, deterministic on all platforms).

Fix (consumer made honest, no payload rollback): _completion_section now keys on the record's own verdict (`str(sidecar.get("verdict")).upper() == "PASS"`) — robust across old (criteria-less) and new FAIL records; the findings-fallback rendering contract is preserved. Added test_completion_fail_with_criteria_still_renders_as_fail pinning the new FAIL-with-criteria shape renders the FAIL panel with findings surfaced (the genuine consumer-graph gap). Mutant check: reverting the keying to the shape proxy is killed by both the pre-existing and the new test.

Also folded in (operator-directed): INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_REMEDIATION now steers against the observed misclassification anti-pattern — search exhaustion is not refutation; make evidence cheaply discoverable via an UNTAGGED ticket comment citing exact test function names, file paths, and merge SHAs, then re-verify; do NOT tag code-verifiable criteria [operator-attested] (reserved for inherently-external evidence). Test extended to pin that guidance.

PS2 amended onto current origin/main (rebased over db4449c821). Local gates: 148 affected tests green (audit page + all 122 targeted), make lint / make typecheck / complexity ratchet clean.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Follow-up (fix b) to creatable-foldable-arthropods (fix a, Gerrit 1761). At SEARCH EXHAUSTION, `BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE` banks `met=false` ("criterion unmet") when the run only established "budget ran out before sufficient evidence was found" — misattributing absence-of-evidence as evidence-of-absence, producing false FAIL verdicts on tickets whose evidence exists but was not reached within the window.

## Proposed fix
Distinguish THREE evidence outcomes: met, refuted, insufficient (search exhausted without a determination) — the third carried as a framework-set `evidence_sufficient:false` marker riding alongside `met:false`, per the verdict_obtainable precedent, so every fail-closed consumer stays unchanged. Marker origin — the banking WRITE path:
- `CompletionEvidencePolicy.fallback_record` (completion_tool_policy.py:100-101) passes a literal `False` through the bool-only record tool. Widen the STRUCTURAL contract: the `fallback_record` Callable (:78) gains the marker; completion_banking's wiring supplies a marker-aware bank write. Not the model-facing tool; keeps the no-completion_banking-import independence (:93-96).
- `CriterionBank.upsert` (:441-461) — persists the optional marker alongside bool `met` (docstring updates).
- `record_criterion_verdict` (:539) stays BOOL; its :544 instruction changes semantics: today it banks `met=false` at the bounded-COMMIT boundary for "not demonstrated" — absence-of-evidence banked as refutation. New rule: `met=false` ONLY on positive refutation; not-found records nothing — the bounded fallback (completion_tool_policy.py:187) fires at the boundary and banks the marker. ALL absence-of-evidence flows through the framework's marker path; the marker is never a model-tool input.
- `harvest_structured_into_bank` (:563-591) keeps its bool gate; the model never emits the marker, so harvest sources it by PRESERVATION: overwrite retains the prior entry's marker — only the widened fallback contract sets it; a genuine refutation (bare met=false) replaces it.

**Full consumer graph (changes together):**
- **Schema (completion_verdict.schema.json)**: per the `verdict_obtainable` precedent (schema :14-18, completion.py:516) — a marker alongside {PASS, FAIL}, not a third token. Two OPTIONAL framework-set markers: `criteria[].evidence_sufficient:false` (exhaustion, not refutation) and top-level `evidence_sufficient:false` (derived: no criterion genuinely unmet, ≥1 insufficient). verdict/met vocabularies unchanged; only message renderers read the marker. Both rendering seams validate against this schema (completion_recovery.py:674, :774).
- **`_validate_coverage` (completion_recovery.py:364-368, :717)**: met stays bool → gates unchanged; markers survive validation.
- **`_run_finalizer` (completion_recovery.py:741)**: banked-evidence payload carries the marker so the finalizer sees exhaustion, not refutation.
- **Unbanked/exhausted placeholders** (`assemble_deterministic_verdict` :646-660, `merge_finalizer_with_bank` :715+): a never-banked criterion at exhaustion IS absence-of-evidence — placeholders carry the marker (keeping `exhausted`), not a bare high-severity FAIL.
- **`reconcile_verdict` (completion.py:495-564)**: `:522` normalization UNTOUCHED. As the single chokepoint both verdict kinds pass through (:561) it DERIVES the top-level marker (set iff no criterion genuinely unmet and ≥1 carries the per-criterion marker); the `:564` remediation branch becomes marker-aware (insufficient-evidence remediation, not unmet-criteria guidance). The `:526` fault path is unaffected.
- **Close-gate refusal (close_precheck.py:571-589)**: still gates on non-PASS (fail-closed) — with the marker present it reports "insufficient evidence" + remediation instead of "N unmet criteria".
- **Standalone verb renderer** `_render_verdict_text` (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:660-693): hard-codes "N unmet criteria" (:672-673) — same marker-aware wording split; exit codes unchanged.
- **Finalizer prompt (completion_verifier_finalizer.md:23-28)**: currently collapses missing/truncated evidence into `met:false` + high-severity FAIL finding. New rule: banked insufficient entries echo as `met:false` with insufficient findings text; `merge_finalizer_with_bank` re-stamps the marker from the bank (stamp = enforcement, prompt = text alignment).
- **Completion sidecar**: the FAIL payload (:355-369) whitelist omits `criteria`; top-level markers ride only via explicit lines (verdict_obtainable :374-375). Add the explicit `evidence_sufficient` line + per-criterion markers to the FAIL payload; round-trip test.
- **Banked-entry rendering** (`assemble_deterministic_verdict` :619-640, `merge_finalizer_with_bank` :705-714): marker-carrying entries emit `met:false + evidence_sufficient:false` with an insufficient-evidence finding, not a bare unmet-criterion FAIL. `merge_finalizer_with_bank` is the authoritative per-criterion RE-STAMP site: the bank (not model output) is the marker's source of truth. Its existing-record branch (:700-704) never consults `bank_entries` — add a bank lookup so the merge overwrites the finalizer's echo (the :705+ fallback already reads the bank). Honesty of message and recorded class, never gate leniency.

## Scope
- Banking WRITE path: `fallback_record` contract + wiring (completion_tool_policy.py); completion_banking.py: `upsert` (persists marker), `record_criterion_verdict` (bool signature unchanged), `harvest_structured_into_bank` (preserve-on-overwrite above), both placeholder branches, `merge_finalizer_with_bank` re-stamp (both branches).
- src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json — optional markers (top-level + per-criterion), verdict_obtainable pattern.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — `_validate_coverage` markers survive validation; `_run_finalizer` payload carries the marker (:741).
- src/rebar/llm/completion.py — `reconcile_verdict` derives the top-level marker + :564 remediation branch marker-aware.
- src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py — refusal message keys on the marker (insufficient evidence vs unmet criteria); still refuses both.
- src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py — `_render_verdict_text` marker-aware wording (:672-673); exit codes unchanged.
- completion_verifier_finalizer.md — sufficiency rule (:23-28).
- src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py — explicit marker lines + criteria in the FAIL payload; round-trip test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At exhaustion, banked fallback evidence carries `evidence_sufficient:false`, never bare `met=false`; unit test.
- [ ] A fallback-banked insufficient entry keeps its marker after a marker-less successor re-harvest (preserve-on-overwrite); genuine refutation (bare met=false) replaces it; model-facing tool stays bool-only; unit tests.
- [ ] Genuine refutation still banks bare `met=false` → FAIL; under the new :544 rule not-found records nothing and the bounded fallback banks the marker; guard tests.
- [ ] Both rendering seams emit `met:false + evidence_sufficient:false` for insufficient entries, INCLUDING their unbanked/exhausted placeholder branches; per-seam and per-branch tests.
- [ ] Schema validates marker-carrying AND all-bool records; `_validate_coverage` passes markers, rejects untyped; `_run_finalizer` payload carries the marker; `merge_finalizer_with_bank` re-stamps from the bank over model echoes; FAIL sidecar round-trips both marker levels; unit tests each.
- [ ] Close gate still BLOCKS on insufficient evidence (verdict stays FAIL) but the refusal — and `_render_verdict_text`'s standalone output — reports insufficient evidence + remediation, not unmet criteria; `reconcile_verdict` derives the top-level marker and swaps remediation; gate + reconcile + renderer tests.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1) before close.

## Out of scope
Guard/memo interaction (fix a, landed); retry policy; prompt changes OTHER than the finalizer's evidence-sufficiency rule above.
